title: eng-ml
text:
eng-ml

alex: Quick heads-up — onboarding run for Janus v1 (baseline fp16) vs q5_k microbatch show a locale-specific regression. When input mixes zh-yue (Cantonese) fragments and Arabic RTL phrases, output drops BLEU and bracket mirroring flips.
mari: ugh. repro script?
alex: repro steps in thread below. Short summary: float16 BLEU=31.2 / COMET=0.82, q5_k BLEU=28.7 / COMET=0.77 on our polyglot subtitle set. But the noisy cases are mostly when a nonbreaking-space/NBSP is present between CJK and Arabic segments and when the tokenizer assigns same token id to different grapheme clusters (vocab shadowing).
li-wei: can you paste the minimal example?
alex: sure:
```
INPUT: "廣東話：早晨سَلام (0xA0 between) 今天天氣如何？"
FP16: "早晨 سَلام。今天天氣如何？"
Q5_K: "早晨سَلام)今天 天氣？"
```
mari: that looks like both spacing and bracket orientation messed up. Does tokenizer map NBSP differently under q5_k quantized weights?
samir: quant shouldn't change tokenizer but pruning/merge ops could be different if we changed token vocab or merges during model export. Did we update vocab or tokenizer merges for Janus?
alex: janus onboarding included a small vocab trim: removed 4k low-frequency merges to speed inference. I think that's the shadowing — a shortdedicated prefix now collides with an Arabic combining cluster.
emily: eval-bot crunched diffs.
eval-bot: Automated delta report:
- dataset: polyglot-subtitles-v2 (n=3,224)
- fp16 BLEU: 31.2 -> q5_k BLEU: 28.7 (delta -2.5)
- fp16 COMET: 0.82 -> q5_k COMET: 0.77 (delta -0.05)
- Regression concentrated in: zh-yue + ar mixed examples (231 samples), and whitespace/NBSP boundary cases (412 samples).
- Shortlist: token-id collisions at vocab indices [11023,11024] correspond to ZWSP/NBSP adjacent merges.
mari: can we bisect whether it's tokenizer/vocab or quant kernels? Suggest: run fp16 model with Janus->tokenizer-trimmed and fp16 with original tokenizer. If delta persists, it's vocab.
li-wei: I'll run that. Also propose a small patch: restore the 4k merges with a targeted exception for NBSP/ZWSP clusters. Should be quick.
samir: Also try fp16 with the trimmed tokenizer but using the compiled kernels from q5_k export (to rule out compile-time reordering).
emily: tagging @mari @li-wei for priority — this will affect dedicated private customers in APAC.
alex: thanks. Patch plan: 1) li-wei run the two fp16 experiments and post diffs. 2) if vocab is root cause, update tokenizer merges and run q5_k smoke. 3) if not, samir will trace kernel export options.
mari: ack. I'll update the onboarding checklist to include a locale-mix smoke for CJK+RTL.
li-wei: starting run now, ETA ~12m. will upload metrics snapshot when done.
alex: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
